why_chain.text: There is no company-specific move to explain in the window. Friday's +0.66% was mostly market and sector (company-specific part +0.21 points, z=0.12), and the -2.9% week was mostly sector (-2.02 points). The ladder below explains the larger 3-month rise (+28.38%) instead, which is where the stock 'stands'.

The stock rose about 28% in 3 months and 46% in 6 months, mostly through two earnings jumps: about +17% on 2026-05-28 after Q2, and a rise of more than 3% after Q3 on 2026-08-26. Both times results beat estimates and full-year guidance went up.

Results beat because growth sped up: Q3 core growth was 7.3%, Life Sciences and Diagnostics grew 10% core, and pharma revenue grew 12%. Book-to-bill (new orders divided by shipments) was above 1 for the 10th quarter in a row, so orders are still arriving faster than Agilent ships.

Pharma growth comes from two sources. First, labs are replacing ageing liquid chromatography (LC) instruments (LC grew at a low-double-digit rate). Second, drug makers are building capacity for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs: GLP-1-related revenue grew more than 70%. Management also points to drug makers moving manufacturing back to the US (reshoring), which it calls a possible $1 billion opportunity through 2030.

Basic driver: pharma companies had held back on lab equipment spending in 2023-2024. They are now upgrading old instruments and adding factory testing capacity for big new drug classes (GLP-1) and US manufacturing. Every new or upgraded instrument also brings years of consumables and service sales (the razor-and-blades pattern in the thesis).
why_chain.evidence: inference (medium): the replacement-cycle and GLP-1 links are sourced to the Q2/Q3 coverage; the 2023-2024 spending pause and the size of the replacement backlog are not sourced in this research

products.name: Liquid chromatography (LC) systems, e.g. the Infinity III / InfinityLab family
products.what_it_is: A lab machine that separates a liquid sample into its individual ingredients so each one can be identified and measured.
products.analogy: Like a race track for molecules: different molecules run through a packed tube at different speeds, so they cross the finish line one by one and can be counted.
products.buyers: Pharma and biotech quality-control and R&D labs (checking drug purity), contract drug manufacturers (CDMOs), food, environmental and chemical testing labs.
products.how_it_works: A pump pushes the dissolved sample through a column packed with tiny particles. Each compound sticks to the particles to a different degree, so they come out at different times, and a detector (or a mass spectrometer, in LC-MS) measures each one. Every run uses columns, solvents and vials, which Agilent also sells through CrossLab.
products.sales: not disclosed by product line. Management said LC grew at a low-double-digit rate in Q3 FY2026, and instrument revenue overall grew at a high-single-digit rate.
products.sales_source: Labelled proxy: Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets segment revenue (which contains LC) was $746M in Q3 FY2026, +10% core [Agilent Q3 FY2026 release, 2026-08-26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1090872/000109087226000062/exhibit991-q326pressrelease.htm). Growth commentary: [Yahoo Finance call highlights, 2026-08-27](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/agilent-technologies-q3-earnings-call-230418624.html)
products.stage: shipping; in a customer replacement (upgrade) cycle
products.size_for_company: The LDG segment (LC, mass spectrometry, cell analysis, diagnostics) was $746M of the $1.88B Q3 revenue, about 40%. LC's own share is not disclosed.
products.competition: Waters (the main LC rival), Thermo Fisher, Shimadzu (not researched in detail today)
products.why_investors_care: The replacement cycle is the engine behind 2026's guidance raises, and each installed instrument pulls through recurring consumables and service revenue.
products.watch_next: Q4 FY2026 results (expected late November 2026): does LC growth stay double-digit, and does book-to-bill stay above 1?

products.name: Agilent 4150 / 4200 TapeStationDx systems and TapeStationDx software
products.what_it_is: Clinical-grade versions of Agilent's automated machine that checks the quality of DNA and RNA samples before they go into genetic sequencing.
products.analogy: A quality inspector at the factory door: it checks the DNA 'raw material' is intact before an expensive sequencing run, so the lab does not waste the run.
products.buyers: Regulated clinical labs running next-generation sequencing (NGS) tests, e.g. cancer genetic testing, in the US, Canada and select European markets.
products.how_it_works: Automated electrophoresis: an electric field pulls DNA/RNA fragments through a gel tape, and their size and integrity are read in about 1-2 minutes per sample. The 4150 handles 1-16 samples and the 4200 handles 1-96. They carry the CE-IVD label (approved for diagnostic use in Europe under the IVDR rules), and the software adds audit trails and electronic signatures.
products.sales_source: Labelled proxy: no product-level figure exists. It sits in the Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets segment, $746M in Q3 FY2026 [Agilent Q3 FY2026 release, 2026-08-26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1090872/000109087226000062/exhibit991-q326pressrelease.htm). Launch facts: [Nasdaq / Agilent release, 2026-09-21](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/agilent-launches-tapestationdx-systems-clinical-ngs-sample-quality-control-2026-09-21)
products.size_for_company: Likely small next to $7.5B of annual revenue (inference, medium). It extends an existing product line into clinical labs rather than creating a new business.
products.competition: not researched today (in this niche, possibly Revvity's LabChip and Thermo Fisher instruments; unverified)
products.why_investors_care: It is a small step in moving research instruments into regulated diagnostics, where products tend to stay in use for longer. It does not move the stock.
products.watch_next: Any mention of clinical adoption on the Q4 call
